hbar:
hbar(data, title, xlabel, ylabel)
Creates and displays a horizontal bar chart. Ideal for rankings or visual comparisons.
- data: pandas.Series with values to plot.
- title: Chart title (str).
- xlabel/ylabel: X and Y axis labels (str).
vbar:
vbar(data, title, xlabel, ylabel)
Creates and displays a vertical bar chart.
- data: pandas.Series with values to plot.
- title: Chart title (str).
- xlabel/ylabel: X and Y axis labels (str).
pie:
pie(values, labels, colors, title)
Creates and displays a percentage pie chart.
- values: array-like with numeric values.
- labels: array-like with names for each category.
- colors: list of colors (RGB or RGBA in hex, e.g. "#FFAA00").
- title: Chart title (str).

normalize:
normalize(data)
Normalizes an array of numeric values between 0 and 1 using min-max scaling.
- data: numpy.ndarray.
Returns: new normalized array (numpy.ndarray).
get_moda:
get_moda(data, with_repetition=False)
Calculates the mode (most frequent value).
- data: numpy.ndarray.
- with_repetition (bool): If True, returns a list with [value, repetition count].
  If False (default), returns only the value.
Ignores NaN by default.
get_media:
get_media(data, nan=False)
Calculates the mean (average) of an array.
- data: numpy.ndarray.
- nan (bool): If True, uses np.nanmean to ignore NaN. Default: False.
Returns: float value with the mean.
get_median:
get_median(data, nan=False)
Calculates the median of an array.
- data: numpy.ndarray.
- nan (bool): If True, uses np.nanmedian to ignore NaN. Default: False.
Returns: float value with the median.

get_var:

- df: DataFrame.
- column: Name of the column.
get_desv:
get_desv(df, column)

histo:

table:
table(data, col_labels, title="")
Creates and displays a visual table from tabular data.
- data: List of lists (e.g. [[value1, value2], ...]) or reduced DataFrame.
- col_labels: List of column labels.
- title: (optional) Title to display above the table.
Uses matplotlib to render a visual summary-style table.
conditional:
conditional(df, conditions, results, column_name)
Applies logical conditions to generate a new column.
- df: Input DataFrame.
- conditions: List of boolean conditions.
- results: List of values to assign when conditions are met.
- column_name: Name of the new column to create.
Uses np.select to evaluate multiple conditions on the DataFrame.
heatmap:
heatmap(df, index_col, column_col, value_col, title="")
Creates a heatmap chart with a cross-tabulation table.
- df: Input DataFrame.
- index_col: Column used as Y axis (index).
- column_col: Column used as X axis (columns).
- value_col: Column whose values are counted to form the matrix.
- title: (optional) Chart title.
Groups, counts and plots with seaborn to visualize density or frequency.
call:
call(name, type=None, path=None, timeout=5, strict=True)
Searches for a file by name (and optionally type) in a given folder (or from cwd) recursively downwards and then upwards,
and loads it depending on its type automatically.

Parameters:
    name (str): Base name of the file, without extension.
    type (str, optional): Expected extension ('csv', 'json', 'xml').
    path (str, optional): Initial path to search from.
    timeout (int, optional): Maximum search time in seconds.
    strict (bool, optional): If True, raises error if multiple files with the same name are found.

Returns: the content of the found file or None.
load_user_translations:
load_user_translations(lang_path="lang.json")
Loads user-defined translations from a JSON file and merges them with the default translations.

Parameters:
    lang_path (str, optional): Path to the user translations file. Defaults to "lang.json".

Behavior:
    - If the file exists and is valid JSON, merges its contents with default translations
    - If the file doesn't exist, keeps only default translations
    - Shows a warning popup if the file exists but can't be loaded
    - Updates the global _translations dictionary

Note: This function must be called before using the t() function for user translations to take effect.
switch:
Enhanced Switch-case system for Python. Supports:
- Multiple matching keys per case
- Match by value, type, regex, lambda function, or class
- Pandas and NumPy data structure support
- Optional async execution of cases
- Match-all mode for executing multiple matching cases
- Debug mode to log matching cases
async_switch:
Wrapper to instantiate Switch in async mode. Parameters:
- value: The value to match against the defined cases.
- **kwargs: Optional keyword arguments passed directly to the Switch class. These can include:
  - match_all (bool): Execute all matching cases instead of stopping at the first.
  - debug (bool): Print which case matched and what executed.
  - async_mode (bool): Should NOT be passed manually here (always forced to True).
Example: AsyncSwitch('hello', match_all=True, debug=True)(...)
